title: Kinetic-inclusive Q3 transfer diagnostic and fourth-power order boundary
question: Can the commuting configuration-order bound be transferred to the kinetic-inclusive Q3 Hamiltonian by a generic fourth-power order shortcut, and what finite Q3 evidence remains after that shortcut is tested?
method: Load the EXP-001192 -> EXP-001191 -> EXP-001190 -> EXP-001189 -> EXP-001188 fixture lineage so couplings, graph volumes, oscillator dimensions and beta values remain single-sourced.
Evaluate the exact 2x2 integer witness A=[[0,0],[0,1]], B=[[1,-2],[-2,4]], K=A+B: A and B are positive semidefinite, K is positive definite, but det(K^4-A^4)=-168.

Rebuild the inherited finite Q3 matrices, set K_full=I+H+|Lambda|r^2/(4g)I and K_pot=I+v(q_0)+v(q_1)+2r^2/(4g)I, and compute direct fourth defects and the generalized quotient ||K_full^-2 K_pot^4 K_full^-2||.
For every inherited volume and beta row, compare finite Gibbs traces Tr(rho K_full^4)-Tr(rho K_pot^4), preserving the finite nature of the diagnostic.
Run independent Python reconstruction and Lean R352 determinant arithmetic; keep the analytic common-core, kinetic uniformity and QFT promotion gates explicitly open.
finding: Primary and independent lanes each pass 50/50 assertions over 15 finite volume-beta rows; the integrated verifier passes 22/22 with Lean R352 PASS. The generic witness has K^4-A^4=[[169,-408],[-408,984]], determinant -168 and minimum eigenvalue -0.14568844308544726, so form order alone does not imply fourth-power order. In the declared finite Q3 matrices the direct K_full^4-K_pot^4 defects are positive with minima 4.859077918599313 (V=2), 38.08487570500183 (V=4), and 188.5990825617291 (V=6); the largest relative quotient is 0.24309945427679083 and the largest potential/full fourth moments are 3.9338865788966113 and 2066.1832202572123. These finite observations do not supply a volume- or cutoff-uniform kinetic theorem.
decision_reason: The proposed generic shortcut is exactly fenced off by an integer positive-matrix counterexample, while the actual finite Q3 rows remain a useful diagnostic and show no failure on the declared grid. The next proof obligation is therefore an analytic source-local commutator or graph-norm estimate on a common polynomial core, rather than an unjustified power monotonicity step.

A and B are positive semidefinite, K=A+B is positive definite, and the negative determinant proves K^4-A^4 is not positive semidefinite.
The boundary matches the p^2 versus q-potential noncommutation in Q3; no commuting assumption is inserted into K_full.
Direct defects, relative quotients and Gibbs traces are reported on the registered grid only; finite positivity is not extrapolated to uniformity.
The inverse-square congruence is retained as a finite diagnostic and is not promoted to an unbounded common-core estimate.
R352 checks exact determinant arithmetic only; Python supplies matrix spectra and all analytic-domain/limit assertions remain open.
No kinetic transfer, Gibbs uniformity, direct history, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A is closed.
